output.name: *Skalun* — "the Lamp Under the Keel"
output.myth: Tirun came home keel-up in the spring gale, with no crew aboard and her lamp still lit underneath. Hesk went down the tally at the pole and found eleven names missing and no reel that had let them go. Tavo laughed when the old women asked him. He had only lifted the boat, he said. Aun, who cut the string, would not say what he had seen. Ennu came with bone and cloth and turned the hull over to look. Under the planks sat a lamp, trimmed by someone careful, and nobody in the islands can say whose hands. So the boat hangs in Vel with its light under the keel. Naskel the Drift-Log watches it from twelve degrees north, the pale trunk that rode a south wind, and keeps quiet, knowing what the sea takes. Sixteen degrees east, the Lit Shoal burns where nine fishers stayed past dark. When the wind is wrong, the old ones say, you can see that light moving beneath the hull, like someone still bailing, still counting, still looking for the way home.
output.finding: Find the Drift-Log, the pale trunk on the Lamp Road, then look a little more than a fist (about 12°) due south of it for the hull, its light showing under the keel.
